purpose: Lumateperone is used to treat schizophrenia in adults. It is also used to treat depressive episodes in adults who have bipolar disorder (either bipolar I or bipolar II). It helps improve mood, thinking, and behavior.
how_it_works: Lumateperone works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain, including serotonin and dopamine. When these chemicals are out of balance, they can cause symptoms like hallucinations, mood swings, or depression. This medication helps bring those chemicals back into a healthier balance so you feel better.
common_side_effects: Sleepiness or drowsiness, dizziness, nausea, and dry mouth are the most common side effects. Some people may also notice increased appetite or feel unusually tired. These effects are often mild and may get better as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious drop in blood pressure when you stand up quickly, so rise slowly to avoid dizziness or fainting. It may increase blood sugar levels, so let your doctor know if you have diabetes. Older adults with dementia-related psychosis should NOT use this medication as it can increase the risk of death. Tell your doctor right away if you experience uncontrolled muscle movements, high fever, or stiff muscles. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 42 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day with food. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed, at the same time each day. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
